sonnet.problem: Card 10 asks the same fact as card 9. Verse 28 says God is the priests' inheritance and that they get no possession in Israel. Card 9's answer ('God Himself') already gives away the true/false answer, so card 10 re-asks something the baker has just been shown.
sonnet.rule: An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact. Two lines that make the same point get one question. An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card.

sonnet.problem: The question already spells out the answer by describing teaching ('showing them the difference between the holy and the common, and the clean and the unclean'). The wrong answers 'soldiers' and 'farmers' are not believable for priests in that sentence, so the right one stands out.
sonnet.rule: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. / A choice card's question never holds its own answer, or a form of it
